title.value: Monitor coding agent progress with periodic reports

introduction.value: The author uses Codex as a hands-off monitor that sends plain-language progress reports every 30 minutes on an implementation agent and can pass messages directly to another agent.

method.value: The author keeps their implementation work in a separate Codex task and sets up another task as a progress monitor. That monitor is scheduled to check in every 30 minutes, send plain-language summaries of what the implementation agent is doing, say whether steering is needed, and, if so, pass a steering prompt directly to the other task via task-to-task messaging instead of making the person interrupt the main worker.

outcome.value: It helped the author stay hands-off and avoid derailing the implementation agent with constant interruptions. In comments, they say the setup also reduces copy-pasting, but they give no hard performance numbers and note context management is still a constant struggle.

notes.value: The main catch they mention is context bloat: split work too finely and agents waste effort on handoffs; keep tasks too large and they start forgetting earlier rules.

source_text.body:
Monitor coding agent progress with periodic reports
The author uses Codex as a hands-off monitor that sends plain-language progress reports every 30 minutes on an implementation agent and can pass messages directly to another agent.
Done with
CX
Codex
What they did
The author keeps their implementation work in a separate Codex task and sets up another task as a progress monitor. That monitor is scheduled to check in every 30 minutes, send plain-language summaries of what the implementation agent is doing, say whether steering is needed, and, if so, pass a steering prompt directly to the other task via task-to-task messaging instead of making the person interrupt the main worker.
How it went
It helped the author stay hands-off and avoid derailing the implementation agent with constant interruptions. In comments, they say the setup also reduces copy-pasting, but they give no hard performance numbers and note context management is still a constant struggle.
Worth knowing
The main catch they mention is context bloat: split work too finely and agents waste effort on handoffs; keep tasks too large and they start forgetting earlier rules.
Try it yourself
with
Codex
Copy prompt
Watch the work happening in [repo, branch or terminal session] and every 30 minutes write me a short plain-language progress report covering what changed, what is stuck and what looks risky. Keep going until [the PR is merged or a stop time], and do not edit any code yourself or send messages to other agents without showing me the message first.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/codex/comments/1v1puqa/task_to_task_messaging_is_underrated
